item.title: AWS Security Hub extends unified security management to Google Cloud Platform
item.description:
Today, AWS announces that AWS Security Hub now monitors Google Cloud Platform (GCP) resources, extending risk analytics, cloud security posture management, vulnerability management, and security response management across both clouds. Many AWS customers running workloads in AWS and GCP have had to operate separate security tools for each environment, making it difficult to prioritize risks holistically or respond consistently. Security Hub now provides a single, unified experience to detect and respond to risks across your AWS and GCP environments in addition to existing support for monitoring Microsoft Azure environments.

Security Hub automatically discovers GCP resources, including GCP Virtual Machines (VMs), GCP Google Artifact Registry (GAR) container images, GCP Cloud Run functions, and GCP identities, and evaluates them for misconfigurations, internet exposure, and software vulnerabilities. You receive posture checks against security standards including the CIS Benchmarks™ for Google Cloud Platform Foundations, unified resource inventory, risk and exposure analysis, and automated response through existing EventBridge integrations. AWS and GCP findings appear in the same prioritized view with the same finding formats and automation workflows, so security teams can operate from one console rather than switching between tools.

Security Hub includes an independent 30-day free trial to monitor GCP resources that begins once you create your integration with Google Cloud Platform. After the trial, you pay the same price for monitoring GCP resources and equivalent AWS resources. You can create an integration to GCP from all AWS Regions where Security Hub is available except Middle East (UAE), Middle East (Bahrain), Asia Pacific (Taipei), and Asia Pacific (New Zealand). You can also create integrations to Google Cloud Platform for AWS Security Hub CSPM for posture management checks and Amazon Inspector for vulnerability management independently from AWS Security Hub. To learn more, see AWS Security Hub Pricing and AWS Security Hub documentation.

item.title: Amazon ECR now replicates image deletions across regions and accounts
item.description:
Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) now supports replicating image deletions and tag removals to your replication destinations. Previously, ECR replication copied images to destination regions and accounts but did not replicate deletions, requiring you to manage deletions separately in each location. With replication of deletes, your destination repositories stay consistent with the source automatically.

Teams running multi-region or multi-account architectures no longer need to script or manually track image cleanup across every destination. When you delete an image or remove a tag in your source registry, whether directly or through a lifecycle policy, ECR propagates that deletion to each destination in the replication rule. Replicated deletions emit EventBridge events and are recorded in CloudTrail, so you have the same visibility into deletions as you do for image pushes.

Replication of deletes is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon ECR is available, at no additional cost. To get started, update your replication configuration in the Amazon ECR console or AWS CLI. For more information, see the Amazon ECR User Guide.

item.title: Amazon EBS now supports associating additional KMS keys with snapshots
item.description:
Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) now supports associating additional AWS Key Management Service (KMS) keys with EBS snapshots. This new capability enables you to share and copy encrypted snapshots across accounts without first re-encrypting them, simplifying your disaster recovery and backup workflows.

Customers use EBS snapshots as durable, point-in-time backups of EBS volumes. By associating an additional customer-managed KMS key (CMK) with a snapshot encrypted with an AWS managed key (AMK), for example, you enable cross-account sharing for that snapshot without re-encrypting its data. This feature accelerates your disaster recovery workflows and enhances operational efficiency for enterprise backup administrators and disaster recovery teams.

Support for associating additional KMS keys with Amazon EBS snapshots is available in all AWS commercial, China, AWS GovCloud (US), and AWS European Sovereign Cloud (Germany) Regions, plus AWS Local Zones and AWS Outposts. You can access this capability through the AWS Console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), and AWS SDKs. To learn more, see the Amazon EBS documentation.
